aliases: headache attributed to traumatic injury to the head
taxonomyDisposition.rationale: ICHD-3 classifies headache attributed to trauma or injury to the head as a secondary headache disorder. A new headache temporally related to head trauma remains classified as trauma-attributed headache even when its phenotype resembles migraine or tension-type headache. Therefore this identity must remain distinct from migraine-headaches.

subtypeModel.acute: Headache attributed to traumatic injury to the head that resolves within 3 months or has not yet persisted for 3 months.
subtypeModel.persistent: Headache attributed to traumatic injury to the head that persists for more than 3 months.
subtypeModel.mildTraumaticInjurySubtype: Use the ICHD-3 mild traumatic injury criteria when the source condition is mild-tbi.
subtypeModel.delayedOnset: Do not make delayed-onset (>7 days to 3 months) part of the default core publication guard. ICHD-3 treats delayed-onset criteria as Appendix criteria; any use should be separately modeled and labeled.

mappingDisposition.publicationGuard: Require documented mild traumatic brain injury plus a new headache developing within the ICHD-3 temporal attribution window. For core ICHD-3 publication, headache onset should be within 7 days after injury, regaining consciousness, or discontinuation of medication that impaired the ability to sense/report headache. Persistent subtype requires duration greater than 3 months.
mappingDisposition.phenotypeBoundary: Migraine-like phenotype does not convert post-traumatic headache into the catalog migraine-headaches diagnosis. Preserve a separate migraine diagnosis only when independently documented or when a pre-existing primary migraine disorder is separately diagnosed.
mappingDisposition.pathwayIntelligence: Do not introduce additional mechanistic pathwayIntelligence solely from PMID 38568491. The relationship is supported through etiologic diagnostic attribution, not a proven single biological mechanism.
mappingDisposition.sourceHandling: Move the existing PMID 38568491 source row from mild-tbi -> migraine-headaches to mild-tbi -> post-traumatic-headache. Do not duplicate it. Keep verified:false during taxonomy/mapping implementation because citation verification remains a separate qualified-human approval step.

currentMismatchDisposition.reason: The source supports post-traumatic headache attributed to mild traumatic brain injury. It notes frequent migraine-like phenotype overlap, but does not establish that the post-traumatic headache diagnosis is equivalent to the catalog migraine-headaches diagnosis.
currentMismatchDisposition.provenance: Preserve the prior mismatch and its resolution in implementation/status documentation, but do not retain the old PMID as an active source on the migraine-headaches relationship.
